title: Expanded original-release SCB poll validation
findings: Three older election years are now admitted using original-release SCB May facts: 2002, 2006 and 2010.
A common-seven panel covers seven elections and five rolling holdouts; a separate extended-eight panel covers five elections and three rolling holdouts.
Unknown/approximate early SD estimates remain missing. No pseudocount or invented new-party history is used.
Each holdout uses only earlier election residuals. Marginal coverage, all-party joint coverage, central-90% interval score and CRPS are reported for all fixed models.
Production Monte Carlo profiles and the previous four-election experiment remain unchanged.

limitations: The seven-party panel excludes SD and OTHER; its scale is not the eight-party production scale. The panels are not scored against each other.
Missing/approximate SD points in 2002 and 2006 are not imputed. Eight-party coverage starts in 2010.
Seven/five elections and five/three rolling test elections remain a small, dependent historical sample. Parties are not independent elections.
May-to-September residuals combine survey error and campaign change. They are not election-day polling errors.
Original-release facts were transcribed from currently accessible official documents. Original downloaded bytes and independently archived historical real-time accessibility are not established.
SCB current Vid10 values for 2010–2019 were retrospectively revised after the 2020 weighting adjustment and are excluded from original-vintage training.
Historical data span changing poll methods, party systems and campaigning. Exchangeable residuals, Gaussian CLR form and fixed shrinkage are modeling assumptions.
Parameter uncertainty is not included in the intervals; small training samples can make them overconfident. Joint coverage refers to all marginal intervals, not a simultaneous-90% band.

This national-composition validation uses the declared CLR estimates without the native stress service sigma<=0.2 cap. Learned scales can exceed 0.2; they are not installed as valid native stress profiles.
Previously inspected 2022/2026 outcomes are development data, not new blind holdouts. No model is selected after these scores, and no production default is changed.
Newly added national vote counts do not validate full district allocations for 2002, 2006 or 2010.
pending: Independent historical-access verification and external replication.
More test elections and genuinely prospective evaluation.
